newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH GRAIN DEMAND, IMPORTS SEEN DOWN IN 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: POLISH GRAIN DEMAND, IMPORTS SEEN DOWN IN 1996/97.

text.p: The Polish government's food market regulator, the Agriculture Market Agency (ARR), said grain imports in the 1996/97 growing season were likely to fall along with a decline in domestic demand, it said on Thursday.

The ARR said grain imports would fall to between one and 1.3 million tonnes in the 1996/97 growing season, running from July to June, from 1.8 million in 1995/96, as internal demand falls to 25.1 million tonnes from last year's 26.5 million.

The agency said in a statement that domestic demand would decline because of decreasing need for fodder grains, whose consumption was expected to fall to 15.2 million tonnes in 1996/97 from 16.9 million tonnes.
The ARR said grain exports would remain flat at 400,000 tonnes in the 1996/97 growing season.
In the July-September period of this year Poland already imported about 480,000 tonnes of grain, including 290,000 tonnes of wheat, the ARR said.
The ARR said the country's grain reserves would increase to 2.4-2.9 million tonnes by June 1997 from 2.2 million last July.
The agency's forecasts were based on prelimanary 1996 grain harvest results released by the Central Statistical Office (GUS) late last month.
GUS said Poland's grain output this year would be between 24.2 and 25.0 million tonnes, down from 25.6 million in 1995.
